items.title: David Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2022
items.q: But I mean I’m going to look at it like let’s say Stanley Kubrick. He’s like one of the best filmmakers we ever had.

ctx.x: And my friend told me one kid got up and said, “My name is so-and-so and I want to be an innovator.” And I was like — and he laughed. He was telling me a joke. Like look at these kids, what the? And he’s a kid, he’ll grow up, he’ll figure it out but it’s interesting that some people think that’s how it happens. Or people who are being considered in that realm play with that realm a little bit. You know. It’s an interesting phenomenon. But I mean I’m going to look at it like let’s say Stanley Kubrick. He’s like…

based realms the changes are going to be more subtle and I don’t think people will hear it. I mean a lot of things that are considered innovation these days are more, you’re kind of hitting somebody over the head. The changes have to be bigger for people to recognize them. And I think in the realm of, I think Sonny Rollins spent fifty years perfecting his craft you know. Was he an innovator? I think so at the beginning, but he still kept going. You know? I think it manifests itself in different ways and more…
